source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Houston (HOU3-HOU4) publishes 84 MW of IT capacity across 347,000 square feet of technical space. At a nominal 40 kW per rack, this represents roughly 2,100 racks. At 6-8 racks per 1-megawatt-equivalent of accelerator clusters, that is approximately 260 to 420 GPU-scale units, assuming standard AI training density; the actual accelerator count depends on whether the operator sells as general compute or AI-specific configurations, which is not published.

This campus ranks first by published capacity among 19 facilities with disclosed megawatt figures in Texas, and among 133 mapped data center sites in the state. Its 84 MW represents 18 percent of the 475 MW of IT capacity the state has published. The campus holds a Green Globes certification, which qualifies it for customers requiring that standard. The grid operator, tenancy, available power beyond IT load, and wholesale pricing are not published.

Houston's rank and share reflect either genuine concentration of AI-grade capacity in this campus or uneven disclosure; most mapped facilities in Texas publish no capacity figure. Arrival of major accelerator tenants or expansion beyond 84 MW would materially shift the state's usable capacity, but no forward plans are published. This site matters most as a reference point for AI demand in Texas, not yet as proof of it.
